findings.evidence: FiniteOrder.lean:96-98 has `have hpoly := Polynomial.isBigO_cobounded_of_degree_le (P := (1 : Polynomial ℂ)) (Q := p) ... simpa using hpoly.mul (isBigO_refl f (cobounded ℂ))`; PoleCleared.lean:229-232 repeats it with `Q := d.polarPolynomial`. A grep for an OrderLE polynomial-division lemma in TauCeti/Analysis finds only `isFiniteOrder_polynomial_mul_iff`.
findings.fix: Add `orderLE_polynomial_mul_iff {p : ℂ[X]} (hp : p ≠ 0) : OrderLE (fun z ↦ p.eval z * f z) A ↔ OrderLE f A` to `Analysis/Complex/FiniteOrder.lean`, derive `isFiniteOrder_polynomial_mul_iff` from it, and use its forward direction here.
findings.issue: The last step of `orderLE_poleClearedContinuedL` proves inline that if `p · f` has order at most `A` and `p ≠ 0`, then so does `f`. It repeats almost word for word the proof of `isFiniteOrder_polynomial_mul_iff`, and no order-level version of the fact exists.

findings.evidence: In PoleCleared.lean:164-186 the only record-specific facts used are `entireCompletion_def` and `meromorphicNFOn_toMeromorphicNFOn`. TauCeti/Analysis/Meromorphic/Order.lean:127 `theorem _root_.Filter.BoundedAtFilter.meromorphicOrderAt_nonneg` already contains the `not_isBoundedUnder_of_tendsto_atTop`/`tendsto_cobounded_of_meromorphicOrderAt_neg` argument.
findings.fix: Make it a public general lemma such as `OrderLE.eventually_analyticAt_cobounded {f : ℂ → ℂ} (hf : MeromorphicNFOn f Set.univ) (hA : OrderLE f A) : ∀ᶠ z in cobounded ℂ, AnalyticAt ℂ f z` under `Analysis/Complex`, prove it with `BoundedAtFilter.meromorphicOrderAt_nonneg`, and apply it to `d.entireCompletion`.
findings.issue: The private `eventually_analyticAt_entireCompletion` is stated for `d.entireCompletion` but uses only that it is in meromorphic normal form and has order at most `A`. Its inline argument (bounded near a point, so the order there is nonnegative) repeats the existing `Filter.BoundedAtFilter.meromorphicOrderAt_nonneg`.

summary: The new theorems are stated at the right level, but two helper steps are proved only for this record when they hold in general: polynomial division preserving order is re-proved inline, and the no-poles-off-a-bounded-set lemma is specialized to `d.entireCompletion`.
